analysis:
The units are documentation-only changes: docs/provider/troubleshooting.md (a date bump, a new drain-failure row at head line 134, a selected-model retry row and a restart-needed row at head lines 167-169) and the head-side tail of docs/provider/cli-reference.md (paths, config keys, env passthrough, runtime constants). The cli-reference patch excerpt also shows new text about drain behavior with the coordinator connection down, a 10s session wait, a 15s per-model unload wait and an enabled_models restart notice. No executable code, keys, authorization checks, attestation paths or encryption behavior change in the supplied evidence.

Security-relevant claims the docs make, which I could not verify against source:
(1) A drain with no coordinator session finishes with 'coordinator acknowledgement: not needed' after 10s. The docs reason that the disconnect already cancelled accepted work. Adjacent: T-010 (cancellation) and TB-002 (coordinator-to-provider boundary). The actual ProviderLoop.performLifecycleDrain was not supplied.
(2) Shutdown abandons a model whose native retirement never finishes after 15s and leaves it to process exit. This is relevant to T-028, residual GPU memory, but process exit reclaims memory. The implementation was not supplied.
(3) Selected-model recovery evicts only idle models outside the selection that carry no Autopilot hold, pin or lease. This touches A-018 availability and T-059-style holds. The implementation was not supplied.
(4) The listed cache env vars (DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE and related) describe defaults consistent with T-041 and do not appear to alter them. The excerpt does not show these as changed. The SSD cache TTL and budget statements in the docs were not changed here.

No new attack surface or threat-model invalidation is evident. The next pass should confirm the code changes behind these docs, if any, in ProviderLoop lifecycle drain, unloadAllModelsForShutdown and the selected-model recovery, especially that fail-closed behavior and admission refusal during the drain are preserved.
